title: DOTr eyes barrier-less tollways pilot testing before end of 2026
summary: The Department of Transportation is eyeing to implement a barrier-less tollways system across all toll roads before the end of the year.

blocks.text: The Department of Transportation (DOTr) is eyeing to implement a barrier-less tollways system across all toll roads before the end of the year.

In an order, Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon said the plan is “in line with our shared commitment to modernizing our road networks, eliminating bottlenecks at toll plazas, and delivering a seamless, world-class travel experience for the motoring public.”
With this, Dizon said that the full implementation of a “Barrier-less/Multi-Lane Free Flow (MFF) Program” across all expressways has become an “urgent national priority.”
“To achieve these benefits, we are targeting the pilot test/proof of concept of the MLFF Program across all expressways before the end of this year,” the Transportation chief said.
Dizon further said that the success of a barrier-less system relies heavily on “near-universal” adoption of cashless payments and “robust backend infrastructure.”
Thus, the DOTr ordered toll roads operators to submit a comprehensive “Action Plan and Readiness Assessment” for the expressways under their jurisdiction.
The following key components should be included in the submission:

• Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) Penetration Strategies: Concrete, time-bound initiatives to aggressively increase RFID/ETC adoption among motorists (e.g., expanded installation sites, digital onboarding, promotional incentives, and public information campaigns)

• Infrastructure and Technology Readiness: Current status and deployment timelines for gantries, Automatic Number/License Plate Recognition (ALPR/ANPR) cameras, high-speed RFID readers, and system integration
• Operational and Enforcement Protocols: Proposed mechanisms for handling non-registered vehicles, insufficient balances, and interoperability across different expressway operators
• Implementation Timeline and Milestones: A month-by-month roadmap detailing testing phases, dry ruins, and target dates for full live operation.

“Given the tight timeline and the immediate need to alleviate traffic congestion for our commuters, kindly submit your comprehensive report to this office on or before 21 December 2026 through the Toll Regulatory Board,” Dizon said.
The Transportation chief said that transitioning to a barrier-less system is “no longer merely an operational upgrade; it is an economic necessity.”

“By removing physical toll barriers, we can significantly reduce travel time, lower fuel consumption and carbon emissions caused by idling vehicles, and maximize the overall throughput and efficiency of our expressway infrastructure,” he said. —KG, GMA News
